texts.preamble: Hasanali Sulemanbhai Sunsara vs State Of Gujarat on 18 March, 2026 R/Cr.Ra/627/2013 Judgme In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Revision Application (Against Order Passed By Subordinate Court) No. 627 of 2013 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar ============================================ Approved for Reporting Yes ============================================ Hasanali Sulemanbhai Sunsara & Anr. Versus State Of Gujarat ============================================ Appearance: Mr Ashish M Dagli(2203) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2 Mr Rohan Raval, App for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ============================================ Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar Date : 18/03/2026 Judgment
texts.facts: Hence, the present Revision Application is filed by the applicants-accused.
texts.arguments: 2) Learned Advocate for the applicants has submitted that both the Courts have committed error in convicting the applicants by relying on Rule 29 of the Act and misinterpreted the provisions of Sections 7 and 16 of the Act. The said rule is applicable to limited articles so far sample of chana masala sabji is concerned synthetic colour is permissible and as per Rule 29 synthetic colour is permissible no offence is made out. Further no proper sample was collected and committed error in relying the conviction and sentence. There was no violation of Rule 29 and hence requested to allow the present application. He has further NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/627/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined submitted to consider provisions of Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act and requested to modify the sentence by taking a lenient view. 3) Learned APP for the respondent - State has submitted that both the Courts have not committed any error as sunset yellow synthetic food colour was found which violates Rule 29 which is not permissible. In such circumstances, in light of the judgment in Nemi Chand v. State of Rajasthan, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/627/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined reported in (2018) 17 SCC 448, and Triloki Chand v. State of Himachal Pradesh, reported in (2020) 10 SCC 763, as per which in cases where the article is found to be substandard, only penalty in the form of fine is required to be imposed.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2) Learned Advocate for the applicants has submitted that both the Courts have committed error in convicting the applicants by relying on Rule 29 of the Act and misinterpreted the provisions of Sections 7 and 16 of the Act. The said rule is applicable to limited articles so far sample of chana masala sabji is concerned synthetic colour is permissible and as per Rule 29 synthetic colour is permissible no offence is made out. Further no proper sample was collected and committed error in relying the conviction and sentence. There was no violation of Rule 29 and hence requested to allow the present application. He has further NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/627/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined submitted to consider provisions of Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act and requested to modify the sentence by taking a lenient view.
